investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so no agent pod reached a running state and the eval produced zero evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption explicitly ruled out by the scheduler, every remote-agent pod creation attempt timed out unscheduled (~133–147 s per check). Because no pod ever started, the eval runner could not collect orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-confirmed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

expected-output.contract: assertions require vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-259); neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was returned.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all existing remote-agent VMs are occupying the available slots and none have been released, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource entirely or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector (e.g., a node label or taint required for peer-pod scheduling is absent), permanently reducing the schedulable node count to 2.
[Possible] A prior eval run or user-created remote agent was not cleaned up and is holding a VM slot, reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe agent.
[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or nodes were drained/cordoned, reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously higher count.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod's node affinity or resource request (e.g., requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than any single node can provide) could cause permanent unschedulability independent of current load.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the required kata peer-pod VM because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner cannot collect any of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity (0 allocatable units remaining), and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, the pod remains Unschedulable for ~133–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so no agent pod reached a running state and the eval produced zero evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption explicitly ruled out by the scheduler, every remote-agent pod creation attempt timed out unscheduled (~133–147 s per check). Because no pod ever started, the eval runner could not collect orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-confirmed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, latencyMs=151442, endedAt=2026-06-19T14:41:35.358Z — confirms the condition persisted for at least ~7 minutes.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=139937 — the check ran for ~140 s before failing, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold defined in infra/evals/status/features.json:183, confirming the failure is a scheduling block rather than a latency breach.

expected-output.contract: assertions require vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-259); neither assertion could be evaluated because no evidence was returned.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all existing remote-agent VMs are occupying the available slots and none have been released, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource entirely or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector (e.g., a node label or taint required for peer-pod scheduling is absent), permanently reducing the schedulable node count to 2.
[Possible] A prior eval run or user-created remote agent was not cleaned up and is holding a VM slot, reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe agent.
[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or nodes were drained/cordoned, reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously higher count.

[Lower likelihood] A misconfiguration in the pod's node affinity or resource request (e.g., requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than any single node can provide) could cause permanent unschedulability independent of current load.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity (0 allocatable units remaining), and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, the pod remains Unschedulable for ~133–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned and the eval probe never reached the runtime layer.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. Because the agent pod never starts, the eval runner (run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent) cannot create the agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is ever produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 147s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable message (133s stuck), endedAt 2026-06-19T14:36:37.741Z — the earliest check in the sequence also failed with the same scheduler rejection.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message (143s stuck), endedAt 2026-06-19T14:39:03.916Z — the intermediate check also failed before runtime was attempted.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence keys returned, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state and the probe never executed past createAgent.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at pod scheduling before any API response could be captured.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: line 1918 shows 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)' — this call is the first step that triggers pod creation; a scheduling failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151442 — the probe waited ~151 seconds before failing, consistent with the scheduler timeout reported in the message (147s stuck).
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster has a fixed quota of peer-pod VM slots on those nodes and all slots are currently occupied by existing agents or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a specific node label (e.g., a kata/peer-pods capable node pool) but 4 of 6 nodes no longer carry that label, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may have left agent pods running that were not cleaned up, exhausting the resource before this eval run began.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the node pool with kata.peerpods.io/vm support may not have been scaled to meet concurrent demand from both eval probes and real workloads.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect allocatable vs. requested/used kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all 6 nodes to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify leaks or zombie agents
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Identify any stuck, running, or terminating pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been released.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect node labels to verify which nodes match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm which of the 6 nodes carry the label required by the pod's node affinity/selector, and verify the 4 non-matching nodes have not lost required labels.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for pending remote-agent pods in the cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Identify any pods stuck in Pending state that are holding or competing for kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks failed with the same Unschedulable scheduler message citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector targeting
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe
affectedAreas.reason: The probe produces no evidence (failed-check.evidence is empty) because createAgent cannot return an agent when the pod is Unschedulable.
affectedAreas.details: Lines 1913–1918: the probe branch that calls createAgent and collects evidence; it never advances past pod creation when scheduling fails.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence), so the contract fails entirely.
affectedAreas.details: Lines 266–270: requiredEvidence [orgId, agentId, model, provider, message] and assertion message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura'.

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents feature
affectedAreas.reason: Both required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are failing, which meets the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold for the remote-agents feature.
affectedAreas.details: Lines 183–185: remote-agent-create (required), remote-agent-state (required), remote-agent-runtime (not required). degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes immediately to confirm exhaustion and determine how many slots are occupied.
Audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources for leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user sessions; terminate any that are no longer needed to free capacity.

Investigate why 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector — verify whether those nodes previously carried the required label and whether a node pool change or label drift has occurred.
Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool needs to be scaled out (more nodes or higher per-node VM quota) to handle concurrent eval probe runs alongside real workloads.

Review the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (referenced at line 1916) to confirm it reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources after each eval run, preventing slot leakage across runs.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false in features.json (line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and both are failing — with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, the remote-agents feature is at or past the outage threshold; treat this as a feature-level outage signal for the remote-agents area.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or has self-resolved; a pass with non-empty evidence would indicate transient exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the resource is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm to detect leaks
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies zombie or leaked agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared infrastructure failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks fail with the same scheduler message, confirming a shared infrastructure root cause rather than an isolated probe defect.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check for pending pods in the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Reveals whether other workloads are also stuck pending, indicating a broader cluster capacity problem beyond just the eval probes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — this would rule out resource exhaustion as the cause.

A successful remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime eval run with non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId present) immediately after this failure — this would indicate a transient scheduling blip rather than sustained exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude nodes that previously matched — this would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to a configuration change.
Cluster autoscaler logs showing a scale-up event that resolved the kata.peerpods.io/vm shortage — this would confirm the cause was capacity but also that it self-healed.
A passing run of remote-agent-create sibling check with no changes to the cluster — this would suggest the failure was intermittent and not a persistent capacity ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check result rather than a timeout.
Add a node-affinity-health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, alerting when the eligible node count drops below a minimum threshold.
Add a leaked-pods eval that counts remote-agent pods in non-terminal states (Running, Pending) older than a configurable TTL, catching resource leaks before they exhaust scheduling capacity.
Add a cluster-capacity eval that monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization as a percentage and warns before full exhaustion, giving operators time to scale out before evals begin failing.
